speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, I am Dr. Agent. You have presented with a two-day history of fever and altered mentation; can you describe exactly how your thinking and consciousness have changed during this time?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (NMS). The combination of fever, altered mental status, and a history of haloperidol use for tics is highly suggestive of NMS; I recommend immediate admission for supportive care and measurement of creatine kinase (CK) levels to confirm the diagnosis.
